messages:

Cc: Acme IT Security <security@acme-fin.com>

Subject: SIG follow-up — on-prem/offline evidence delivery

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for walking us through the SIG responses yesterday. Our procurement and security teams reviewed the answers and requested a short addendum that describes how Redwood would handle artifact delivery and ongoing support for an on-prem / air-gapped deployment. Specific asks: 

- How do you deliver artifacts (builds, certificates, audit logs) to an air-gapped environment?
- What options do you offer for periodic offline updates (e.g., quarterly patch bundles)?
- What support model applies when network-based debugging isn't possible (SLA escalations, on-site support, secure courier)?
- Please confirm any additional attestations you can provide (hashes, signed manifests, chain-of-custody).

Can you send a short addendum and an outline of logistics so we can get legal & procurement moving? Ideally something we can attach to the SIG packet by EOD Friday.

Best,
Beth
Beth Harris
Senior Security Program Manager
Acme Financial

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Harris <beth.harris@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — on-prem/offline evidence delivery

Beth,

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. I'm drafting an addendum now. High-level approach we'll include:

• Artifact delivery: encrypted bundles on physical media (FIPS-compliant USB / external SSD) shipped via bonded courier OR air-gapped transfer via customer-controlled transfer node (customer pulls from a locked SFTP endpoint we provision temporarily). All artifacts delivered with SHA-256 hashes and a signed manifest (PKI).

• Offline updates cadence: customizable; default is quarterly patch bundles with emergency hotfix channels. Bundles include binaries, release notes, migration guidance, and verification scripts.

• Support model: remote support by default with pre-shared diagnostic bundles (no inbound connectivity). For cases where remote debugging is impossible, options: scheduled on-site visits (terms by contract), or secure lab-based reproduction coordinated under NDA. We also offer a paid managed-delivery option where Redwood courier-escorts a locked device to the customer's facility.

• Chain-of-custody & attestations: manifests signed by Redwood Release Manager, per-bundle hash lists, and optional notarized handover receipts.

I'll attach a draft addendum and a short checklist for deployment logistics. If this is directionally correct I can loop in Legal/Procurement for final wording.

– Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SIG_Addendum_Acme_v1.pdf (draft addendum), onprem-deployment-checklist.xlsx

Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 09:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — on-prem/offline evidence delivery

Mina / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft — couple commercial/legal notes before we send: 

1) On-site support and courier-escort options need a pricing matrix and an SLA attachment. Suggest we propose: 
   - Standard: remote-only, included in Support Gold (4h business response for Sev 1 via offline bundle exchange).
   - Premium: on-site within 3 business days (per-visit fee + travel).
   - Managed delivery: ticketed courier service with chain-of-custody certificate (annual subscription).

2) For the temporary SFTP transfer node, we should add a sentence that the node is provisioned for a limited window, IP allow-listing is used, and all credentials are rotated post-transfer. Point of contact for provisioning should be the customer's infra lead.

3) Legal will want explicit wording on liability for physical media loss — recommend we state that Redwood uses bonded couriers and takes commercially reasonable care, and that acceptance of media is documented by signed receipt on transfer.

If these look OK I'll draft a short commercial paragraph we can append to the addendum.

Aditya
VP Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Beth — attaching the finalized addendum and a concise logistics checklist. Highlights below and in the addendum: 

1) Artifact delivery options (pick one):
   A) Physical media via bonded courier: encrypted USB/SSD + PKI-signed manifest + notarized receipt.
   B) Customer-pull: temporary, locked SFTP endpoint (credentials rotated post-transfer).

2) Update cadence: standard quarterly bundles, emergency hotfixes as needed. All bundles signed and checksummed; verification script included.

3) Support & escalation: remote-first support with pre-shared diagnostic workflows. On-site visits available under Premium support (3 business day target) or as ad-hoc professional services. Managed-delivery subscription available for high-security environments.

4) Attestations: SHA-256 hashes for all delivered files, manifest signed by Redwood Release Manager, optional notarized chain-of-custody on request.

Next steps we suggest for procurement: confirm preferred delivery option (A or B), indicate if on-site or managed-delivery will be required, and confirm the internal contact for receiving media. Once you confirm, Legal will issue a short SOW/addendum mapping pricing.

Attachments: SIG_Addendum_Acme_v1.pdf, onprem-deployment-checklist.xlsx, sftp-instructions.txt

Thanks — we can also jump on a 20-min call if helpful.
